   108	\section{The source assertion and the obstruction}
   109	
   110	We examine the final step of the subsection ``Applying the classical
   111	low-degree test'' in the analysis of the Pauli basis test in the compression
   112	paper of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen (MIP$^{*}$=RE,
   113	arXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low
   114	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%
   115	\footnote{Tracked in \localissue{0002}.  In the mirror of the source
   116	consulted here, the polynomial-pair lemma and its proof are at
   117	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   118	lines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined
   119	line lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization
   120	with its divisibility, the index function, the soundness statement with its
   121	proof, and admissibility are at
   122	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
   123	lines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}
   124	There, the combined point measurements
   125	$\{\hat Q^{x,z,\alpha,\beta}_c\}$ and combined line measurements
   126	$\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, indexed by points of $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in
   127	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low
   128	individual degree game with parameters
   129	\[
   130	  \mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)
   131	  \tag{\path{lem:qld-4-7}}
   132	\]
   133	of value $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem
   134	for that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.
   135	The two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution
   136	over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
   137	
   138	The game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an
   139	admissible field size \emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not
   140	incidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution
   141	in which a uniform seed coordinate $s \in \F_q$, read as an integer in
   142	$\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique
   143	$\chi(s)$ with
   144	\[
   145	  s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m'} + r, \qquad 0 \le r < \frac{q}{m'},
   146	  \tag{\path{eq:chi-func}}
   147	\]
   148	so that the $m'$ classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ partition $\F_q$ into sets of equal
   149	size $q/m'$ and the index is uniform.  For $m' \nmid q$ neither the index
   150	function nor the line-point distribution built from it is defined.
   151	
   152	Admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$
   153	is a power of two, $m \mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \ge 1$ the integer
   154	$m+1 \ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and
   155	divides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for every
   156	admissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is
   157	undefined for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$: for instance
   158	$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \nmid 8$.  The source performs
   159	the instantiation without addressing the divisibility, so its proof route
   160	establishes the polynomial-pair lemma, and with it the soundness theorem for
   161	the Pauli basis test that rests on it, only for $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.
   162	
   163	\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
   164	\label{sec:import-obligations}
   165	
   166	The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
   167	$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
   168	proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
   169	simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
   170	test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
   171	authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
   172	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
   173	that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
   174	and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
   175	simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither
   176	the asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the
   177	import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
   178	which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as
   179	open.  Both obligations are independent of the divisibility question: they
   180	arise at every dimension, for the $\chi$-based game where it is defined and
   181	equally for the directly indexed variant proposed under the candidate
   182	repairs.
   183	
   184	\paragraph{The cited test.}
   185	In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
   186	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness
   187	measure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of
   188	three subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each
   189	subtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \emph{Axis-parallel lines
   190	test}: sample a uniform point $u \in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis
   191	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\ell$ through $u$ in
   192	direction $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \in \mathcal C$;
   193	send $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff
   194	$g(u_j) = a$.  \emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample
   195	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$ and a subcube $H \subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the
   196	last $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly
   197	in $H$ and a uniform order bit; send the ordered pair $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ to
   198	one prover, who answers a pair $(b_u, b_v)$ of field values; send $u$ to
   199	the other, who answers $a$; accept iff $b_u = a$.  \emph{Synchronicity
   200	test}: send one identical question --- a line, a point, or an ordered
   201	pair, with probability $1/3$ each --- to both provers and accept iff their
   202	answers agree.  Theorem~4.7 supposes a two-prover strategy passing this
   203	test with probability $1-\eps$ together with an integer parameter
   204	$K \ge 12 m' t$, where $t$ is the interpolation parameter of the base code
   205	--- for the degree-$d$ Reed--Solomon code, of blocklength $n = q$ and
   206	distance $q-d$, one has $t = d+1$ --- and produces projective measurements
   207	$\{G_c\}$ and $\{\tilde G_c\}$ with outcomes in $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$,
   208	consistent with one prover's points measurements, with the other prover's
   209	lines measurements, and with each other, up to
   210	$\eta'(m',t,K,\eps,n^{-1}) = \mathrm{poly}(m',t,K) \cdot
   211	\mathrm{poly}(\eps, n^{-1}, e^{-K/(m')^2})$.
   212	
   213	\paragraph{Obligation 1: the game correspondence.}
   214	The source asserts that the $\chi$-based game at parameters $(q,m',d,1)$
   215	is this test.  It is not, in four respects.
   216	(i)~The game has no pair questions.  A pair question of the test reveals
   217	two points of a \emph{hidden} subcube --- the subcube itself is not sent
   218	--- and is answered by two field values, while the game's diagonal-line
   219	question reveals a full line description and is answered by a degree-$m'd$
   220	polynomial.  A reduction must construct the pair measurements from the
   221	diagonal-line measurements by post-processing (measure a line through $u$
   222	and $v$ and evaluate the answered polynomial at the two parameters), and
   223	both directions of the information mismatch matter: the game's line
   224	description carries an index and a seed, neither of which is a function of
   225	the pair $(u,v)$, so the constructed measurement must average over the
   226	compatible indices and seeds; and the game's diagonal lines fix the
   227	\emph{first} $i-1$ coordinates where the test's subcubes fix the
   228	\emph{last} $j-1$, so the coordinate conventions must be aligned.  The
   229	construction must preserve projectivity and must match the law of the
   230	hidden-subcube pair with the law induced by the game's diagonal sampling.
   231	(ii)~The game's line questions carry the seed $s \in \F_q$; the test's
   232	carry only the line.  A strategy may depend on the seed beyond its class
   233	$\chi^{-1}(i)$, and removing this dependence runs into the fiber-averaging
   234	difficulty made explicit under the candidate repairs: averaging preserves
   235	the line-versus-point branches exactly but not the synchronicity branches.
   236	(iii)~The branch weights differ: each nontrivial cross-test has mass $1/3$
   237	in the test against $2/9$ in the game.  Once the per-branch predicates are
   238	matched, the intended bookkeeping bound is that the constructed strategy's
   239	rejection probability in the test is at most $\tfrac32$ times the game's
   240	rejection probability, up to the $O(1/(m'q))$ of item~(iv); this bound is
   241	the target of the obligation, not an established fact.
   242	(iv)~The game's predicate fixes an acceptance convention on diagonal
   243	questions with zero direction --- an event of probability at most
   244	$2/(m'q)$, recorded in the blueprint's remark on zero directions --- for
   245	which the test has no counterpart branch.
   246	Finally, the displayed conclusions of Theorem~4.7 pair one prover's points
   247	measurements with the other prover's tensor-codeword measurement, and the
   248	first prover's tensor-codeword measurement with the second prover's lines
   249	measurements, while the game-level statement asserts the point consistency
   250	in both directions; deriving the stated form uses the role symmetrization
   251	of the test and belongs to the correspondence.  None of these steps is
   252	difficult to state, but none is carried out in the source, and together
   253	they replace the asserted one-line identity by a reduction carrying its
   254	own value bound.
   255	
   256	\paragraph{Obligation 2: the parameter bound.}
   257	Theorem~4.7 requires $K \ge 12 m' t = 12 m' (d+1)$.  The source
   258	instantiates $K = (m')^3 d$, which meets the bound iff
   259	$(m')^2 d \ge 12(d+1)$: this holds for all $d \ge 1$ when $m' \ge 5$,
   260	holds at $m' = 4$ exactly when $d \ge 3$, and fails for every $d$ when
   261	$m' \le 3$.  In the game's parameter domain the dimension divides the
   262	admissible field size and is therefore a power of two, so the source's
   263	instantiation violates the hypothesis exactly at $m' \in \{1,2\}$ for
   264	every $d$ and at $m' = 4$ for $d \in \{1,2\}$ --- in particular, in the
   265	multilinear regime $d = 1$, at every dimension $m' \le 4$.  A candidate
   266	repair is to instantiate $K = \max((m')^3 d,\, 12 m'(d+1))$; the open
   267	obligation is then to re-absorb the error, that is, to check that
   268	$\mathrm{poly}(m',t,K)$ and $e^{-K/(m')^2}$ still collapse to the form
   269	$a(dm')^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bm'd})$ in the small-$m'$ cases where the
   270	maximum is $12m'(d+1)$ --- plausible, since there
   271	$e^{-K/(m')^2} = e^{-12(d+1)/m'}$ decays in $d$ at a rate comparable to
   272	$2^{-m'd}$ for $m' \le 4$, but not checked here.
   273	
   274	In the correspondence of Obligation~1, the only role of the divisibility
   275	$m' \mid q$ is to make the $\chi$-sampled index uniform.  The underlying
   276	mathematics does not need the divisibility.  The low
   277	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} samples its axis
   278	index $i$ uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly, with no index function
   279	on $\F_q$ and no divisibility hypothesis,%
   280	\footnote{See the test figure in \path{references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex}.}
   281	and the tensor-code test is likewise a test about the code
   282	$\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$, not about an encoding of indices into $\F_q$.  The
   283	$\chi$-based packaging exists so that the question distribution is
   284	conditionally linear, which the introspection machinery requires for the
   285	game the players actually play --- the Pauli basis test at dimension $m$,
   286	where admissibility does supply the divisibility.  The game at dimension
   287	$2m+2$ never appears in a verifier; it is an internal analysis device in the
   288	proof of the polynomial-pair lemma, so nothing there requires its question
   289	distribution to be conditionally linear.
   290	
   291	\section{Candidate repairs}
   292	
   293	\paragraph{Direct index sampling (candidate direction, recommended).}
   294	Define, for arbitrary $m' \ge 1$, the line-point distribution over
   295	$\F_q^{m'}$ that samples the uniform point, the uniform axis index
   296	$i \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first
   297	$i-1$ coordinates, directly; define the \emph{directly indexed game} with
   298	this question distribution, whose line questions carry the index $i$ (and,
   299	for diagonal lines, the projected direction) in place of the seed
   300	$s \in \F_q$; and state the imported soundness theorem for that game
   301	(form~4 above).  This removes the divisibility obstruction and nothing
   302	else: the directly indexed game still asks for polynomials on revealed
   303	lines, has no pair questions, and weighs its branches as the present game
   304	does, so establishing form~4 carries the same two import obligations as
   305	the $\chi$-based import (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}), now at
   306	arbitrary dimension.
   307	
   308	The relation to the present game when $m' \mid q$ must moreover be proved
   309	at the level of games, not merely of question distributions, because the
   310	two games have different question alphabets: an $\mathsf{ALine}$ question
   311	of the $\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0, s)$ and a $\mathsf{DLine}$
   312	question a triple $(u_0, s, v')$, so a strategy may select different
   313	measurements for seeds $s \ne s'$ with $\chi(s) = \chi(s')$, and equality
   314	of the induced laws of the geometric data does not by itself transport
   315	such a strategy.  The transport layer decomposes into the following
   316	obligations, none of which is carried out here.
   317	\begin{itemize}
   318	  \item \emph{Distribution lemma.}  When $m' \mid q$, the image of the
   319	  conditionally linear question distribution under the parsing map
   320	  $(u_0,s) \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s))$, $(u_0,s,v') \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s),v')$
   321	  is the direct distribution, and conditioned on the parsed question the
   322	  seed is uniform on the class $\chi^{-1}(i)$, independently of everything
   323	  else.
   324	  \item \emph{Parsing pullback.}  A strategy for the directly indexed game
   325	  composed with the parsing map is a seed-oblivious strategy for the
   326	  $\chi$-based game.  Since the win predicate depends on the question only
   327	  through the parsed data, and a seed-oblivious strategy answers
   328	  identically across each fiber --- in particular on the synchronicity
   329	  branches, where both players hold the same seed --- the value should be
   330	  preserved exactly on every branch, and projectivity is preserved.  This
   331	  is the direction the combining subtree needs.
   332	  \item \emph{Seed-fiber averaging: what it preserves and what it does
   333	  not.}  In the opposite direction, average each line measurement over its
   334	  seed fiber: attach to a direct question $(u_0,i)$, respectively
   335	  $(u_0,i,v')$, the average over uniform $s \in \chi^{-1}(i)$ of the
   336	  measurements attached to $(u_0,s)$, respectively $(u_0,s,v')$, leaving

   338	  seed this preserves the value of every \emph{line-versus-point} branch

   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}
   441	
   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$

   168	\begin{definition}
   169	Consider the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   170	For $j \in \{1, \ldots, m\}$,
   171	we refer to the \emph{$j$-restricted diagonal lines test}
   172	as the diagonal lines test conditioned on $\bi = j$.
   173	For example, in the $m$-restricted diagonal lines test,
   174	the line $\bell$ is simply a uniformly random line in $\F_q^m$.
   175	\end{definition}
   176	
   177	Now we state our main theorem using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:prelims} below.
   178	This the formal version of \Cref{thm:main-informal}.
   179	
   180	\begin{theorem}[Main theorem; quantum soundness of the low individual degree test]\label{thm:main-formal}
   181	  Consider a projective strategy $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ 
   182	   which passes the  $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test with probability at least $1-\eps$.
   183	  Let $k \geq md$ be an integer.
   184	  Let
   185	  \begin{equation*}
   186	  \nu = 100000 k^2m^4 \cdot \Big(\eps^{1/40000} + (d/q)^{1/40000} + e^{-k/(2560000m^2)}\Big).
   187	  \end{equation*}
   188	Then there exists projective measurements $G^{\mathrm{A}}, G^{\mathrm{B}} \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ with the following properties:
   189	\begin{enumerate}
   190	  \item (Consistency with~$A$):  On average over $\bu \sim \F_q^{m}$,
   191		  \begin{align*}
   192		  A^{\mathrm{A},u}_a \otimes I
   193		  	&\simeq_{\nu} I \otimes G^{\mathrm{B}}_{[g(u)=a]},\\
   194		I \otimes A^{\mathrm{B},u}_a
   195		  	&\simeq_{\nu}  G^{\mathrm{A}}_{[g(u)=a]} \ot I.
   196		  \end{align*}
   197	\item (Self-consistency):
   198		\begin{equation*}
   199		G^{\mathrm{A}}_g \ot I \simeq_{\nu} I \ot G^{\mathrm{B}}_g.
   200		\end{equation*}
   201	\end{enumerate}
   202	\end{theorem}
   203	
   204	We note that there is a tradeoff in \Cref{thm:main-formal} specified by the parameter~$k$.
   205	As~$k$ increases, $\nu$'s prefactor $k^2$ increases.
   206	On the other hand, as $k$ increases, the term $e^{- k/(2560000m^2)}$ which also occurs in $\nu$ \emph{decreases}.
   207	Thus, when applying this theorem, one must select~$k$ to balance these competing demands.
   208	Typically, choosing $k = \poly(m)$ should be more than sufficient for applications.
   209	We believe that this parameter~$k$ is an artifact of our proof,
   210	and we hope that it will be removed in the future.

291	\section{Candidate repairs}
   292	
   293	\paragraph{Direct index sampling (candidate direction, recommended).}
   294	Define, for arbitrary $m' \ge 1$, the line-point distribution over
   295	$\F_q^{m'}$ that samples the uniform point, the uniform axis index
   296	$i \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first
   297	$i-1$ coordinates, directly; define the \emph{directly indexed game} with
   298	this question distribution, whose line questions carry the index $i$ (and,
   299	for diagonal lines, the projected direction) in place of the seed
   300	$s \in \F_q$; and state the imported soundness theorem for that game
   301	(form~4 above).  This removes the divisibility obstruction and nothing
   302	else: the directly indexed game still asks for polynomials on revealed
   303	lines, has no pair questions, and weighs its branches as the present game
   304	does, so establishing form~4 carries the same two import obligations as
   305	the $\chi$-based import (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}), now at
   306	arbitrary dimension.
   307	
   308	The relation to the present game when $m' \mid q$ must moreover be proved
   309	at the level of games, not merely of question distributions, because the
   310	two games have different question alphabets: an $\mathsf{ALine}$ question
   311	of the $\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0, s)$ and a $\mathsf{DLine}$
   312	question a triple $(u_0, s, v')$, so a strategy may select different
   313	measurements for seeds $s \ne s'$ with $\chi(s) = \chi(s')$, and equality
   314	of the induced laws of the geometric data does not by itself transport
   315	such a strategy.  The transport layer decomposes into the following
   316	obligations, none of which is carried out here.
   317	\begin{itemize}
   318	  \item \emph{Distribution lemma.}  When $m' \mid q$, the image of the
   319	  conditionally linear question distribution under the parsing map
   320	  $(u_0,s) \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s))$, $(u_0,s,v') \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s),v')$
   321	  is the direct distribution, and conditioned on the parsed question the
   322	  seed is uniform on the class $\chi^{-1}(i)$, independently of everything
   323	  else.
   324	  \item \emph{Parsing pullback.}  A strategy for the directly indexed game
   325	  composed with the parsing map is a seed-oblivious strategy for the
   326	  $\chi$-based game.  Since the win predicate depends on the question only
   327	  through the parsed data, and a seed-oblivious strategy answers
   328	  identically across each fiber --- in particular on the synchronicity
   329	  branches, where both players hold the same seed --- the value should be
   330	  preserved exactly on every branch, and projectivity is preserved.  This
   331	  is the direction the combining subtree needs.
   332	  \item \emph{Seed-fiber averaging: what it preserves and what it does
   333	  not.}  In the opposite direction, average each line measurement over its
   334	  seed fiber: attach to a direct question $(u_0,i)$, respectively
   335	  $(u_0,i,v')$, the average over uniform $s \in \chi^{-1}(i)$ of the
   336	  measurements attached to $(u_0,s)$, respectively $(u_0,s,v')$, leaving
   337	  the points measurements unchanged.  By the conditional uniformity of the
   338	  seed this preserves the value of every \emph{line-versus-point} branch
   339	  exactly: there the paired question carries no seed, so the branch value
   340	  is an average over the fiber of per-seed values, which the averaged
   341	  measurement computes.  It does \emph{not} preserve the synchronicity
   342	  branches.  There both players hold the same seed, so the $\chi$-based
   343	  branch value is the diagonal average
   344	  $\E_{s}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s)}_f
   345	  \rangle$, while the averaged strategy realizes the double average
   346	  $\E_{s,s'}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s')}_f
   347	  \rangle$ over independent seeds in the fiber; the two differ whenever
   348	  the players' measurements vary across a fiber in a correlated way (if
   349	  both apply a common seed-dependent relabelling, every diagonal term is
   350	  large and the cross terms are not), and neither quantity dominates the
   351	  other in general.  An earlier revision of this note claimed that the
   352	  averaging preserves the exact value, and with it synchronicity; that
   353	  claim was wrong and is withdrawn.  What needs proof is control of the
   354	  synchronicity branches under de-seeding.  Candidate approaches: show
   355	  that a strategy of value $1-\eps$ in the $\chi$-based game is, with
   356	  polynomial loss, close to a seed-oblivious one; or state form~4 with a
   357	  synchronicity hypothesis in the doubled-average form and re-derive it on
   358	  the tensor-code side.  Choosing and proving one of these is an open
   359	  obligation.
   360	  \item \emph{Projectivity round trip.}  The averaged strategy is a POVM
   361	  strategy even when the given one is projective, while the imported
   362	  theorem, like the present one, takes projective strategies.  The
   363	  intended round trip is: dilate the averaged strategy to a projective one
   364	  (Naimark preserves all product correlations
   365	  $\langle X \ot Y \rangle$ of the given strategy against the dilated
   366	  state --- hence the value of every branch the averaging preserved ---
   367	  but nothing restores the diagonal seed correlations once the averaging
   368	  has been performed); apply form~4; and compress the resulting polynomial
   369	  measurement along the dilation isometry back to a POVM in the required
   370	  measurement class on the original space.  That this compression
   371	  preserves the consistency conclusions must itself be proved; it is
   372	  stated here as an obligation, not established.  (Alternatively, form~4
   373	  may be stated for POVM strategies outright, moving the dilation inside
   374	  the import.)
   375	\end{itemize}
   376	
   377	The combining subtree would then be reread with the direct distribution
   378	and the directly indexed game at dimension $2m+2$: every statement becomes
   379	well defined for all admissible tuples, and the expectation is that the
   380	proofs survive unchanged, because the measurements constructed there are
   381	indexed by the geometric data --- points, lines, and polynomials on them
   382	--- and so constitute a strategy for the directly indexed game outright,
   383	with no fiber averaging.  Verifying, lemma by lemma, that those proofs use
   384	only the laws of the sampled objects and never the conditional linearity
   385	of the sampling is part of this direction's obligations.  This follows the
   386	subtree protocol for a definition-level mismatch: the definition is
   387	corrected at the lowest point rather than each downstream lemma acquiring
   388	a hypothesis.  The transport layer costs one parsing-map definition, the
   389	distribution lemma, the pullback lemma, whichever synchronicity control is
   390	chosen, and the dilation--compression lemma; the first three are an
   391	estimated one to two hundred lines on top of the restated import, with the
   392	blueprint's existing Naimark interface supplying the dilation, while the
   393	synchronicity control is the step whose weight is genuinely uncertain.
   394	The external check that the tensor-code test of arXiv:2111.08131 samples
   395	its axes and subcubes directly has been made against that source: Figure~1
   396	there draws the axis index and the subcube data uniformly and directly,
   397	with no index encoding into $\F_q$.
   398	
   399	\paragraph{Padding the dimension.}
   400	Alternatively, embed the combined polynomial into
   401	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,\bar m}(\F_q)$ for $\bar m = 4m$, the least power of two
   402	with $\bar m \ge 2m+2$, ignoring the $2m-2$ dummy variables.  Then
   403	$\bar m \mid q$ holds whenever $q \ge 4m$, and the existing game applies at
   404	dimension $\bar m$.  In the complementary regime $m \in \{q/2,\, q\}$ the
   405	conclusion is vacuous: $md \ge q/2$ gives
   406	$\delta_S \ge a(md)^a q^{-b} \ge a\,2^{-a} q^{a-b} \ge a\,2^{-b} \ge 1$
   407	for $a \ge 2$, while the consistency quantities bounded by the theorem never
   408	exceed $1$.  This route stays inside the present definitions but reworks the
   409	sub-line distribution (a fourth coordinate block of dummies), the combining
   410	map, and the wrong-block Schwartz--Zippel analysis, and it moves the
   411	combining lemmas away from their source statements at dimension $2m+2$.
   412	
   413	\paragraph{Unequal index classes.}
   414	One could instead define an index function at dimension $2m+2$ with classes
   415	of sizes $\lfloor q/(2m+2)\rfloor$ and $\lceil q/(2m+2)\rceil$.  The index
   416	is then only approximately uniform, the identification with the external
   417	test fails exactly, and every distributional identity in the sub-line
   418	analysis acquires an error term; this amounts to re-proving the imported
   419	soundness theorem for a perturbed game and is not recommended.
   420	
   421	\section{Comparison with the blueprint}
   422	
   423	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} keeps the sub-line lemma, the
   424	combined line lemma, and the polynomial-pair lemma in their source-shaped
   425	statements, with no divisibility hypothesis.  Their proofs retain the source
   426	constructions and mark the unresolved obligation at the exact steps: the
   427	first sampling step of the sub-line construction, where $\chi_{2m+2}$ and
   428	the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ are invoked, and the
   429	instantiation step of the polynomial-pair proof, where $(q,2m+2,d,1)$ is
   430	used as a game parameter tuple.  A chapter remark records the divisibility
   431	arithmetic and cites this note; the final soundness theorem for the Pauli
   432	basis test remains open modulo this obligation.  The blueprint's proof node
   433	for the classical soundness import itself states the source's route --- the
   434	identification with the two-prover tensor-code test and the application of
   435	Theorem~4.7 --- and enumerates the two obligations of
   436	Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations} as open, citing this note for the
   437	detailed comparison and the case arithmetic.  An earlier revision had
   438	instead added the hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$ to the three lemmas; that was
   439	statement drift in the sense of the proof-gap protocol, since the hypothesis
   440	excludes all admissible $m \ge 2$ and does not appear in the source.
   441	
   442	\section{Conclusion}
   443	
   444	There is a theorem-level gap in the source proof route: the classical low
   445	individual degree game invoked at dimension $2m+2$ is undefined for every
   446	admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ (and for $(q,m) = (2,1)$), because its
   447	question distribution requires $2m+2 \mid q$ while admissibility supplies
   448	only $m \mid q$.  The cited route therefore does not establish the
   449	polynomial-pair lemma, nor the soundness of the Pauli basis test that
   450	depends on it, beyond $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.  Independently of the
   451	divisibility, the import of the classical game's quantum soundness carries
   452	the two open verification obligations of
   453	Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}: the asserted identity with the
   454	two-prover tensor-code test must be replaced by a reduction carrying a
   455	value bound, and the source's instantiation of the auxiliary parameter
   456	violates the theorem's lower bound at the small dimensions listed there.
   457	We do not assert that any conclusion is false: the underlying tensor-code
   458	soundness is insensitive to how the axis index is sampled, and both import
   459	obligations concern verification, not counterexample.  For the divisibility
   460	repair, the recommended candidate direction is direct index sampling ---
   461	restate the imported soundness theorem for the directly indexed game at
   462	arbitrary dimension; prove the distribution and parsing-pullback lemmas;
   463	settle the synchronicity control for de-seeding together with the
   464	dilation--compression round trip, so that the present soundness statement
   465	would follow from the repaired import; and reread the combining subtree
   466	against the directly indexed game --- a direction whose open obligations
   467	are enumerated under the candidate repairs, not an established route, with
   468	dimension padding as the fallback confined to the present game definition.

   318	
   319	/-!
   320	The diagonal-block conditional expectation preserves either mixed defect
   321	exactly because the point measurement on the opposite carrier is constant on
   322	the residue register.  It does not yield a global/global compression theorem:
   323	the lifted state pairs equal residues, whereas separately compressing both
   324	polynomial measurements produces an independent double average over residues.
   325	Neither quantity bounds the other in general.  This open obstruction is
   326	recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
   327	-/
   328	
   329	/-- The normalized diagonal-block average of an operator on a carrier with a
   330	finite ancillary register.  This is the local conditional expectation used to
   331	discard one half of the correlated seed-residue ancilla. -/
   332	noncomputable def averageDiagonalBlock
   333	    {iota block : Type*} [Fintype iota] [Fintype block]
   334	    (A : Op (iota × block)) : Op iota := by
   335	  classical
   336	  exact (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   337	    ∑ r, A.submatrix (fun i => (i, r)) (fun i => (i, r))
   338	
   339	/-- Compress a POVM through the normalized diagonal-block average.  The
   340	nonemptiness assumption says precisely that the normalized finite average is
   341	defined over at least one ancillary basis element. -/
   342	noncomputable def correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement
   343	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   344	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   345	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block] [Nonempty block]
   346	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block)) :
   347	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota :=
   348	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   349	    (fun a => averageDiagonalBlock (M.effect a))
   350	    (fun a => by
   351	      unfold averageDiagonalBlock
   352	      apply smul_nonneg
   353	      · positivity
   354	      · exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun r _ =>
   355	          Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr
   356	            ((Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp (M.pos a)).submatrix
   357	              (fun i => (i, r))))
   358	    (by
   359	      classical
   360	      ext i j
   361	      simp only [averageDiagonalBlock, Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.smul_apply,
   362	        Matrix.submatrix_apply]
   363	      calc
   364	        ∑ a, (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   365	              ∑ r, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) =
   366	            (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   367	              ∑ a, ∑ r, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) := by
   368	                rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   369	        _ = (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   370	              ∑ r, ∑ a, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) := by
   371	                rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   372	        _ = (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   373	              ∑ r, (1 : Op (iota × block)) (i, r) (j, r) := by
   374	                congr 1
   375	                apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   376	                intro r _
   377	                simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using
   378	                  congrFun (congrFun M.sum_eq_one (i, r)) (j, r)

    29	/-- View the coordinate function of an LDT pure state as a Euclidean vector. -/
    30	noncomputable def pureStateEuclideanVector
    31	    {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota] [Nonempty iota]
    32	    (psi : PureState iota) : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota :=
    33	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm psi.vector

    35	@[simp] theorem pureStateEuclideanVector_apply
    36	    {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota] [Nonempty iota]
    37	    (psi : PureState iota) (i : iota) :
    38	    pureStateEuclideanVector psi i = psi.vector i :=
    39	  rfl

    41	/-- The Euclidean vector associated with an LDT pure state has norm one. -/
    42	theorem pureStateEuclideanVector_norm
    43	    {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota] [Nonempty iota]
    44	    (psi : PureState iota) : ‖pureStateEuclideanVector psi‖ = 1 := by
    45	  have hsquareComplex :
    46	      ((‖pureStateEuclideanVector psi‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) = 1 := by
    47	    calc
    48	      ((‖pureStateEuclideanVector psi‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) =
    49	          (‖pureStateEuclideanVector psi‖ : ℂ) ^ 2 := by norm_cast
    50	      _ = inner ℂ (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)
    51	          (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) :=
    52	        (inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)).symm
    53	      _ = dotProduct psi.vector (star psi.vector) :=
    54	        EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct _ _
    55	      _ = dotProduct (star psi.vector) psi.vector := dotProduct_comm _ _
    56	      _ = 1 := psi.unit
    57	  have hsquare : ‖pureStateEuclideanVector psi‖ ^ 2 = (1 : ℝ) := by
    58	    exact_mod_cast hsquareComplex
    59	  nlinarith [norm_nonneg (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)]

    61	/-- Evaluation in a pure LDT density state is the quadratic form of its
    62	Euclidean vector. -/
    63	theorem pureState_stateQForm_eq_ev
    64	    {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota] [Nonempty iota]
    65	    (psi : PureState iota) (T : Op iota) :
    66	    DistanceCalculus.stateQForm (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) T =
    67	      ev (psi : QuantumState iota) T := by
    68	  rw [PureState.ev_eq_re_inner]
    69	  unfold DistanceCalculus.stateQForm applyOperatorToState
    70	  change (inner ℂ (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)
    71	      (WithLp.toLp 2 (T *ᵥ psi.vector))).re =
    72	    (dotProduct (star psi.vector) (T *ᵥ psi.vector)).re
    73	  rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct, dotProduct_comm]
    74	  rfl

    76	/-- For complete projective families and a pure bipartite state, the mature
    77	LDT consistency relation is exactly the QPBT off-diagonal defect.  In
    78	particular, changing between the density and vector formulations incurs no
    79	loss in the error parameter. -/
    80	theorem consRel_iff_consistencyDefect
    81	    {Question Outcome iotaA iotaB : Type*}
    82	    [Fintype Question] [DecidableEq Question]
    83	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    84	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
    85	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
    86	    [Nonempty (iotaA × iotaB)]
    87	    (psi : PureState (iotaA × iotaB))
    88	    (mu : Distribution Question) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
    89	    (A : Question → ProjMeas Outcome iotaA)
    90	    (B : Question → ProjMeas Outcome iotaB) (delta : ℝ) :
    91	    ConsRel (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
    92	        (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) delta ↔
    93	      consistencyDefect mu
    94	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
    95	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
    96	        (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) ≤ delta := by
    97	  let AM : Question → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (iotaA × iotaB) :=
    98	    fun x => DistanceCalculus.leftPlacedMeasurement
    99	      (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement (A x).toMeasurement)
   100	  let BM : Question → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (iotaA × iotaB) :=
   101	    fun x => DistanceCalculus.rightPlacedMeasurement
   102	      (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement (B x).toMeasurement)
   103	  have hAM (x : Question) (a : Outcome) :
   104	      (AM x).effect a = heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1 := rfl
   105	  have hBM (x : Question) (a : Outcome) :
   106	      (BM x).effect a = heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a) := rfl
   107	  have hdefect :
   108	      consistencyDefect mu
   109	          (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
   110	          (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
   111	          (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) =
   112	        bipartiteConsError (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
   113	          (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) := by
   114	    calc
   115	      consistencyDefect mu
   116	          (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
   117	          (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
   118	          (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) =
   119	          1 - avgOver mu (fun x => ∑ a,
   120	            DistanceCalculus.stateQForm (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)
   121	              ((AM x).effect a * (BM x).effect a)) := by
   122	            simpa only [hAM, hBM] using
   123	              DistanceCalculus.consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap
   124	                mu AM BM (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) hmu
   125	                  (pureStateEuclideanVector_norm psi)
   126	      _ = avgOver mu (fun x => 1 - ∑ a,
   127	            DistanceCalculus.stateQForm (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)
   128	              ((AM x).effect a * (BM x).effect a)) := by
   129	            rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_of_isProbability mu hmu]
   130	      _ = bipartiteConsError (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
   131	          (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) := by
   132	            unfold bipartiteConsError
   133	            apply avgOver_congr
   134	            intro x
   135	            rw [qBipartiteConsDefect_of_measurements
   136	              (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB))
   137	              (A x).toMeasurement (B x).toMeasurement]
   138	            rw [ev_one_of_isNormalized (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB))
   139	              psi.toQuantumState_isNormalized]
   140	            congr 1
   141	            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   142	            intro a _
   143	            rw [hAM, hBM]
   144	            rw [DistanceCalculus.placed_product_stateQForm_eq]
   145	            exact pureState_stateQForm_eq_ev psi
   146	              (opTensor ((A x).outcome a) ((B x).outcome a))
   147	  constructor
   148	  · intro h
   149	    rw [hdefect]
   150	    exact h.offDiagonalBound
   151	  · intro h
   152	    refine ⟨?_⟩
   153	    rw [← hdefect]
   154	    exact h

   214	theorem strategyConsRel_consistencyDefect_le

   216	    {Question Outcome : Type*}
   217	    [Fintype Question] [DecidableEq Question]
   218	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
   219	    (mu : Distribution Question) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
   220	    (A : Question → ProjMeas Outcome S.ιA)
   221	    (B : Question → ProjMeas Outcome S.ιB) (delta : ℝ)
   222	    (h : ConsRel (strategyQuantumState S) mu
   223	      (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) delta) :
   224	    consistencyDefect mu
   225	      (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
   226	      (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a)) S.ψ ≤ delta := by

     4	/-!
     5	# Strategy transport for the directly indexed low-degree game
     6	
     7	This module reads one coordinate of a projective directly indexed strategy as
     8	a two-space mature low individual degree strategy.  The question and answer
     9	transport of `Transport.Questions` supplies the canonical direct question of
    10	every mature line, with the reversed coordinate order and the leading index
    11	of the decoded diagonal direction, together with answer readouts that are
    12	covariant under line rebasing; this establishes all four covariance
    13	conditions of `ProjStrat`.  The module also records exact Born-weight
    14	formulas for both directions of strategy transport.
    15	
    16	## References
    17	
    18	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-458`
    19	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:49-151`
    20	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    21	-/

    34	/-- Regard a matrix-valued projective measurement as a projective measurement
    35	in the mature LDT interface. -/
    36	noncomputable def matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas
    37	    {alpha iota : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    38	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    39	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :
    40	    MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjMeas alpha iota where
    41	  toMeasurement := {
    42	    toSubMeas := {
    43	      outcome := M.effect
    44	      total := 1
    45	      outcome_pos := M.pos
    46	      sum_eq_total := M.sum_eq_one
    47	      total_le_one := le_rfl
    48	    }
    49	    total_eq_one := rfl
    50	  }
    51	  proj a := (hM a).isIdempotentElem.eq

   113	/-- The coordinate axis-line family is independent of the chosen affine
   114	parametrization of a mature line. -/
   115	theorem directCoordinateAxisMeasurement_reparam
   116	    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   117	    {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   118	    (M : DirectLdQuestion D →
   119	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectLdAnswer D) iota)
   120	    (hM : ∀ q, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M q)) :
   121	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   122	    AxisParallelMeasurementReparamInvariant D.toLDTParameters
   123	      (directCoordinateAxisMeasurement D r M hM) := by
   124	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   125	  classical
   126	  intro line t f
   127	  simp only [directCoordinateAxisMeasurement, ProjMeas.postprocess,
   128	    SubMeas.postprocess_outcome, matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome]
   129	  rw [directAxisQuestionOf_rebase]
   130	  have hfiber :
   131	      Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   132	        directAxisAnswerReadout D r (line.rebaseAt t) answer =
   133	          AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAt f t) =
   134	        Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   135	          directAxisAnswerReadout D r line answer = f) := by
   136	    ext answer
   137	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   138	    rw [directAxisAnswerReadout_rebase]
   139	    exact (AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAtEquiv t).injective.eq_iff
   140	  rw [hfiber]

   171	private theorem strategy_carrier_nonempty {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) :
   172	    Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) := by
   173	  by_contra h
   174	  rw [not_nonempty_iff] at h
   175	  letI := h
   176	  have hzero : S.ψ = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
   177	  have hnorm := S.ψ_norm
   178	  rw [hzero, norm_zero] at hnorm
   179	  exact zero_ne_one hnorm

   288	private theorem vectorBornWeight_finset_sum_left
   289	    {alpha iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   290	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   291	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   292	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   293	    (s : Finset alpha) (A : alpha → Op iotaA) (B : Op iotaB) :
   294	    vectorBornWeight psi (∑ a ∈ s, A a) B =
   295	      ∑ a ∈ s, vectorBornWeight psi (A a) B := by
   296	  classical
   297	  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
   298	  | empty =>
   299	      simp [vectorBornWeight, vectorBornAmplitude_zero_left]
   300	  | @insert a s ha ih =>
   301	      rw [Finset.sum_insert ha, Finset.sum_insert ha,
   302	        vectorBornWeight_add_left, ih]

   322	private theorem strategyQuantumState_ev_eq_vectorBornWeight
   323	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (A : Op S.ιA) (B : Op S.ιB) :
   324	    ev (strategyQuantumState S) (opTensor A B) =
   325	      vectorBornWeight S.ψ A B := by
   326	  letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) := strategy_carrier_nonempty S
   327	  rw [show strategyQuantumState S =
   328	      PureState.toQuantumState (strategyPureState S) by
   329	        simp [strategyQuantumState],
   330	    PureState.ev_eq_re_inner]
   331	  unfold vectorBornWeight vectorBornAmplitude applyOperatorToState heteroKron opTensor
   332	  simp_rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
   333	  change (star S.ψ ⬝ᵥ
   334	      (Matrix.kronecker A B *ᵥ S.ψ)).re =
   335	    ((Matrix.kronecker A B *ᵥ S.ψ) ⬝ᵥ star S.ψ).re

   338	/-- Postprocessing both local measurements gives the exact double sum of the
   339	original Born weights over the two answer fibers. -/
   340	theorem directPostprocessBornWeight
   341	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   342	    (hS : S.IsProjective)
   343	    {alpha beta : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha]
   344	    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta]
   345	    (x y : DirectLdQuestion D)
   346	    (readA : DirectLdAnswer D → alpha)
   347	    (readB : DirectLdAnswer D → beta)
   348	    (a : alpha) (b : beta) :
   349	    ev (strategyQuantumState S)
   350	        (opTensor
   351	          ((ProjMeas.postprocess
   352	            (matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas (S.A x) (hS.1 x)) readA).outcome a)
   353	          ((ProjMeas.postprocess
   354	            (matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas (S.B y) (hS.2 y)) readB).outcome b)) =
   355	      ∑ directA ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun answer => readA answer = a),
   356	        ∑ directB ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun answer => readB answer = b),
   357	          outcomeWeight S x y directA directB := by
   358	  rw [strategyQuantumState_ev_eq_vectorBornWeight]
   359	  simp only [ProjMeas.postprocess, SubMeas.postprocess_outcome,
   360	    matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome]
   361	  rw [vectorBornWeight_finset_sum_left]
   362	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   363	  intro directA _
   364	  rw [vectorBornWeight_finset_sum_right]
   365	  rfl

   367	/-- Correlated residue registers turn two block-diagonal effects into the
   368	uniform average of their matching source-block Born weights. -/
   369	private theorem seedFiberBlockBornAmplitude
   370	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams)
   371	    (A : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιA)
   372	    (B : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιB) :
   373	    vectorBornAmplitude (seedFiberLiftedState S L)
   374	        (Matrix.blockDiagonal A) (Matrix.blockDiagonal B) =
   375	      (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
   376	        ∑ residue, vectorBornAmplitude S.ψ (A residue) (B residue) := by
   377	  classical
   378	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   379	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   380	  unfold vectorBornAmplitude applyOperatorToState heteroKron Matrix.kronecker
   381	  simp_rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
   382	  simp only [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_apply,
   383	    dotProduct, Matrix.mulVec]
   384	  simp_rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product]
   385	  simp [seedFiberLiftedState_apply, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply,
   386	    mul_assoc, mul_comm]
   387	  ring_nf
   388	  simp_rw [mul_assoc, ← Finset.mul_sum]
   389	  ring_nf
   390	  simp_rw [mul_assoc, ← Finset.mul_sum]
   391	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   392	  rw [← mul_assoc]
   393	  congr 1
   394	  rw [← pow_two, inv_pow, ← Complex.ofReal_pow,
   395	    Real.sq_sqrt (Nat.cast_nonneg (L.q / L.m))]
   396	  norm_cast
   397	  exact Complex.ofReal_inv _

   399	/-- Correlated residue registers give the uniform average of the source-block
   400	Born weights. -/
   401	private theorem seedFiberBlockBornWeight
   402	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams)
   403	    (A : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιA)
   404	    (B : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιB) :
   405	    vectorBornWeight (seedFiberLiftedState S L)
   406	        (Matrix.blockDiagonal A) (Matrix.blockDiagonal B) =
   407	      (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
   408	        ∑ residue, vectorBornWeight S.ψ (A residue) (B residue) := by

    29	/-- A uniform consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of
    30	its question type. -/
    31	theorem consistencyDefect_uniform_question_equiv
    32	    {X Y Outcome iota : Type*}
    33	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Nonempty X]
    34	    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
    35	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    36	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    37	    (e : X ≃ Y) (A B : Y → Outcome → Op iota)
    38	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    39	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
    40	        (fun x a => A (e x) a) (fun x a => B (e x) a) psi =
    41	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi := by
    42	  unfold consistencyDefect
    43	  simpa using avgOver_uniform_equiv e (fun x =>
    44	    ∑ a : Outcome, ∑ b : Outcome,
    45	      if a = b then 0 else
    46	        (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
    47	          (((A (e x) a) * (B (e x) b)).mulVec psi))).re)
    48	
    49	/-- A consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of both
    50	outcome families. -/
    51	theorem consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv
    52	    {X Alpha Beta iota : Type*}
    53	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
    54	    [Fintype Alpha] [DecidableEq Alpha]
    55	    [Fintype Beta] [DecidableEq Beta]
    56	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    57	    (mu : Distribution X) (e : Beta ≃ Alpha)
    58	    (A B : X → Alpha → Op iota) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    59	    consistencyDefect mu
    60	        (fun x b => A x (e b)) (fun x b => B x (e b)) psi =
    61	      consistencyDefect mu A B psi := by
    62	  unfold consistencyDefect
    63	  apply avgOver_congr
    64	  intro x
    65	  let term : Alpha → Alpha → ℝ := fun a b =>
    66	    if a = b then 0 else
    67	      (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
    68	        (((A x a) * (B x b)).mulVec psi))).re
    69	  calc
    70	    _ = ∑ a : Beta, ∑ b : Beta, term (e a) (e b) := by
    71	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    72	      intro a _
    73	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    74	      intro b _
    75	      unfold term
    76	      by_cases hab : a = b
    77	      · subst b
    78	        simp
    79	      · have heab : e a ≠ e b := fun h => hab (e.injective h)
    80	        simp [hab, heab]
    81	    _ =
    82	        ∑ a : Beta, ∑ b : Alpha, term (e a) b := by
    83	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    84	      intro a _
    85	      exact Equiv.sum_comp e (fun b => term (e a) b)
    86	    _ = ∑ a : Alpha, ∑ b : Alpha, term a b :=
    87	      Equiv.sum_comp e (fun a => ∑ b : Alpha, term a b)
    88	    _ = _ := rfl

    90	/-- Simultaneous bijective relabeling of uniform questions and outcomes leaves
    91	the consistency defect unchanged. -/
    92	theorem consistencyDefect_uniform_question_outcome_equiv
    93	    {X Y Alpha Beta iota : Type*}
    94	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Nonempty X]
    95	    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
    96	    [Fintype Alpha] [DecidableEq Alpha]
    97	    [Fintype Beta] [DecidableEq Beta]
    98	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    99	    (questionEquiv : X ≃ Y) (outcomeEquiv : Beta ≃ Alpha)
   100	    (A B : Y → Alpha → Op iota) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
   101	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
   102	        (fun x b => A (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b))
   103	        (fun x b => B (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b)) psi =
   104	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi := by
   105	  calc
   106	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
   107	        (fun x b => A (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b))
   108	        (fun x b => B (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b)) psi =
   109	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
   110	        (fun x a => A (questionEquiv x) a)
   111	        (fun x a => B (questionEquiv x) a) psi :=
   112	      consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv (uniformDistribution X)
   113	        outcomeEquiv _ _ psi
   114	    _ = consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi :=
   115	      consistencyDefect_uniform_question_equiv questionEquiv A B psi

   119	/-- Pointwise equality of both operator families gives equality of their
   120	consistency defects. -/
   121	theorem consistencyDefect_congr
   122	    {X Outcome iota : Type*}
   123	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
   124	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
   125	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   126	    (mu : Distribution X) (A A' B B' : X → Outcome → Op iota)
   127	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota)
   128	    (hA : ∀ x a, A x a = A' x a) (hB : ∀ x a, B x a = B' x a) :
   129	    consistencyDefect mu A B psi = consistencyDefect mu A' B' psi := by
   130	  unfold consistencyDefect
   131	  apply avgOver_congr
   132	  intro x
   133	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   134	  intro a _
   135	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   136	  intro b _
   137	  by_cases hab : a = b
   138	  · simp [hab]
   139	  · simp only [hab, if_false]
   140	    rw [hA x a, hB x b]

   142	/-- The direct single-coordinate point/global defect is exactly the mature
   143	defect after the polynomial, point, and scalar equivalences. -/
   144	theorem directPointPolynomial_consistencyDefect_eq
   145	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   146	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
   147	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   148	    ∀ (G : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB),
   149	      consistencyDefect
   150	          (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   151	          (fun u a => heteroKron
   152	            ((directPointCoordinateMeasurementA D S r u).effect a) 1)
   153	          (fun u a => heteroKron 1
   154	            ((directPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).effect a)) S.ψ =
   155	        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   156	          (maturePointAPlaced D S hS r)
   157	          (maturePolynomialEvaluationRight D G) S.ψ := by
   158	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   159	  intro G
   160	  calc
   161	    consistencyDefect
   162	        (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   163	        (fun u a => heteroKron
   164	          ((directPointCoordinateMeasurementA D S r u).effect a) 1)
   165	        (fun u a => heteroKron 1
   166	          ((directPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).effect a)) S.ψ =
   167	      consistencyDefect
   168	        (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   169	        (fun u a => maturePointAPlaced D S hS r
   170	          (directPointEquiv D u) (directScalarEquiv D a))
   171	        (fun u a => maturePolynomialEvaluationRight D G
   172	          (directPointEquiv D u) (directScalarEquiv D a)) S.ψ := by
   173	          apply consistencyDefect_congr
   174	          · intro u a
   175	            unfold maturePointAPlaced
   176	            congr 1
   177	            exact (directCoordinatePointMeasurement_effect_transport
   178	              D S hS r u a).symm
   179	          · intro u a
   180	            unfold maturePolynomialEvaluationRight
   181	            congr 1
   182	            exact directPolynomialMeasurement_evaluation_effect D G u a
   183	    _ = consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   184	        (maturePointAPlaced D S hS r)
   185	        (maturePolynomialEvaluationRight D G) S.ψ :=
   186	      consistencyDefect_uniform_question_outcome_equiv
   187	        (directPointEquiv D) (directScalarEquiv D)
   188	        (maturePointAPlaced D S hS r)
   189	        (maturePolynomialEvaluationRight D G) S.ψ

   191	/-- Convert the mature point/global `ConsRel` conclusion to its vector-state
   192	QPBT defect formulation. -/
   193	theorem maturePointPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le
   194	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   195	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
   196	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   197	    ∀ (G : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB)
   198	      (delta : ℝ),
   199	      ConsRel (strategyQuantumState S)
   200	          (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   201	          (fun u => (matureCoordinatePointMeasurementA D S hS r u).toSubMeas)
   202	          (fun u => (maturePolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).toSubMeas) delta →
   203	        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   204	          (maturePointAPlaced D S hS r)

   101	private theorem correlated_ancilla_scale
   102	    (block : Type*) [Fintype block] [Nonempty block] :
   103	    (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card block : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
   104	        (starRingEnd ℂ)
   105	          (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card block : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ =
   106	      (Fintype.card block : ℂ)⁻¹ := by
   107	  rw [show (starRingEnd ℂ)
   108	      (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card block : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ =
   109	        (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card block : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ by simp]
   110	  rw [← pow_two, inv_pow, ← Complex.ofReal_pow,
   111	    Real.sq_sqrt (Nat.cast_nonneg (Fintype.card block))]
   112	  norm_cast
   113	  exact Complex.ofReal_inv _

   115	private theorem correlatedState_compress_left
   116	    {iotaA iotaB block : Type*}
   117	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   118	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   119	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block] [Nonempty block]
   120	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   121	    (phi : EuclideanSpace ℂ ((iotaA × block) × (iotaB × block)))
   122	    (hphi : ∀ i j r s, phi ((i, r), (j, s)) =
   123	      if r = s then
   124	        psi (i, j) * (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card block : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹
   125	      else 0)
   126	    (A : Op (iotaA × block)) (B : Op iotaB) :
   127	    DistanceCalculus.stateQForm phi
   128	        (heteroKron A (Matrix.blockDiagonal fun _ => B)) =
   129	      DistanceCalculus.stateQForm psi
   130	        (heteroKron (averageDiagonalBlock A) B) := by
   131	  classical
   132	  unfold DistanceCalculus.stateQForm
   133	  apply congrArg Complex.re
   134	  unfold applyOperatorToState heteroKron Matrix.kronecker averageDiagonalBlock
   135	  simp_rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
   136	  simp only [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_apply, dotProduct,
   137	    Matrix.mulVec]
   138	  simp_rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product]
   139	  suffices h :
   140	      (∑ i : iotaA, ∑ r : block, ∑ j : iotaB,
   141	        ∑ i' : iotaA, ∑ j' : iotaB,
   142	          (starRingEnd ℂ)
   143	              (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card block : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
   144	            (starRingEnd ℂ) (psi (i, j)) *
   145	              (B j j' * (A (i, r) (i', r) *
   146	                ((Real.sqrt (Fintype.card block : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
   147	                  psi (i', j'))))) =
   148	        ∑ i : iotaA, ∑ j : iotaB, ∑ i' : iotaA,
   149	          ∑ j' : iotaB, ∑ r : block,
   150	            (starRingEnd ℂ) (psi (i, j)) *
   151	              (psi (i', j') * (B j j' *
   152	                ((Fintype.card block : ℂ)⁻¹ * A (i, r) (i', r)))) by
   153	    simpa [hphi, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply, Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply,
   154	      apply_ite, map_zero, ite_mul, zero_mul, Finset.sum_ite_eq,
   155	      Finset.mem_univ, if_true, map_mul, Matrix.submatrix,
   156	      Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.of_apply, Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_mul,
   157	      mul_assoc, mul_comm] using h
   158	  apply Fintype.sum_congr
   159	  intro i
   160	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   161	  apply Fintype.sum_congr
   162	  intro j
   163	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   164	  apply Fintype.sum_congr
   165	  intro i'
   166	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   167	  apply Fintype.sum_congr
   168	  intro j'
   169	  apply Fintype.sum_congr
   170	  intro r
   171	  ring_nf
   172	  rw [correlated_ancilla_scale block]
   173	  ring

    25	/-- Formalization-only definition used in the proof of Fact 4.26: place a
    26	complete measurement on the left tensor factor. -/
    27	noncomputable def leftPlacedMeasurement {α ιA ιB : Type*}
    28	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
    29	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    30	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιA) :
    31	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (ιA × ιB) :=
    32	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    33	    (fun a => heteroKron (M.effect a) 1)
    34	    (fun a => MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg (M.pos a)
    35	      (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg : 0 ≤ (1 : Op ιB)))
    36	    (by
    37	      change ∑ a : α, leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) (M.effect a) = 1
    38	      rw [leftTensor_finset_sum, M.sum_eq_one, leftTensor_one])
    39	
    40	/-- Formalization-only definition used in the proof of Fact 4.26: place a
    41	complete measurement on the right tensor factor. -/
    42	noncomputable def rightPlacedMeasurement {α ιA ιB : Type*}
    43	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
    44	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    45	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιB) :
    46	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (ιA × ιB) :=
    47	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    48	    (fun a => heteroKron 1 (M.effect a))
    49	    (fun a => MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg
    50	      (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg : 0 ≤ (1 : Op ιA)) (M.pos a))
    51	    (by
    52	      change ∑ a : α, rightTensor (ι₁ := ιA) (M.effect a) = 1
    53	      rw [rightTensor_finset_sum, M.sum_eq_one, rightTensor_one])

    55	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for Fact 4.26: products of left and right

    66	/-- The (possibly unnormalized) rank-one state associated to a Euclidean vector. -/
    67	private noncomputable def vectorQuantumState {ι : Type*}
    68	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    69	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : QuantumState ι where
    70	  density := pureDensity ψ.ofLp
    71	  density_psd := by
    72	    refine Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr ?_
    73	    exact (Matrix.posSemidef_vecMulVec_self_star ψ.ofLp).smul
    74	      (by positivity : 0 ≤ (Fintype.card ι : ℂ))

    76	/-- Evaluation in the rank-one vector state is the corresponding quadratic form. -/
    77	private theorem vectorQuantumState_ev_eq_stateQForm {ι : Type*}
    78	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    79	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (T : Op ι) :
    80	    ev (vectorQuantumState ψ) T = stateQForm ψ T := by
    81	  have hcard : (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) ≠ 0 :=
    82	    Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
    83	  change (MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (pureDensity ψ.ofLp * T)).re =
    84	    stateQForm ψ T
    85	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_mul_comm]
    86	  unfold pureDensity MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
    87	  rw [Matrix.mul_smul, Matrix.mul_vecMulVec, Matrix.trace_smul, Matrix.trace_vecMulVec]
    88	  change (((Fintype.card ι : ℂ) *
    89	      ((T *ᵥ ψ.ofLp) ⬝ᵥ star ψ.ofLp)) /
    90	      (Fintype.card ι : ℂ)).re = stateQForm ψ T
    91	  rw [mul_div_cancel_left₀ _ hcard]
    92	  unfold stateQForm applyOperatorToState
    93	  rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
    94	  simp [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_apply]

    96	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for Fact 4.26: postprocessing can only
    97	increase diagonal tensor overlap. -/
    98	theorem diagonal_postprocess_stateQForm_ge {α β ιA ιB : Type*}
    99	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
   100	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
   101	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   102	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB))
   103	    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιA)
   104	    (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιB) (f : α → β) :
   105	    (∑ b : β, stateQForm ψ
   106	        (heteroKron ((A.postprocess f).effect b) ((B.postprocess f).effect b))) ≥
   107	      ∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect a)) := by
   108	  classical
   109	  cases isEmpty_or_nonempty (ιA × ιB) with
   110	  | inl hι =>
   111	      letI := hι
   112	      have hψ : ψ = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
   113	      subst ψ
   114	      simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState]
   115	  | inr hι =>
   116	      letI := hι
   117	      letI : Nonempty ιA := ⟨(Classical.choice hι).1⟩
   118	      letI : Nonempty ιB := ⟨(Classical.choice hι).2⟩
   119	      let HA : FiniteHilbertSpace :=
   120	        { carrier := ιA
   121	          instFintype := inferInstance
   122	          instDecidableEq := inferInstance
   123	          instNonempty := inferInstance }
   124	      let HB : FiniteHilbertSpace :=
   125	        { carrier := ιB
   126	          instFintype := inferInstance
   127	          instDecidableEq := inferInstance
   128	          instNonempty := inferInstance }
   129	      let As : SubMeas α ιA :=
   130	        (MatrixMeasurement.toMeasurement (H := HA) A).toSubMeas
   131	      let Bs : SubMeas α ιB :=
   132	        (MatrixMeasurement.toMeasurement (H := HB) B).toSubMeas
   133	      have hAoutcome (a : α) : As.outcome a = A.effect a := by
   134	        simp [As, HA]
   135	      have hBoutcome (a : α) : Bs.outcome a = B.effect a := by
   136	        simp [Bs, HB]
   137	      have hApost (b : β) :
   138	          (MIPStarRE.LDT.postprocess As f).outcome b =
   139	            (A.postprocess f).effect b := by
   140	        rw [SubMeas.postprocess_outcome,
   141	          MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
   142	        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   143	        intro a _
   144	        exact hAoutcome a
   145	      have hBpost (b : β) :
   146	          (MIPStarRE.LDT.postprocess Bs f).outcome b =
   147	            (B.postprocess f).effect b := by
   148	        rw [SubMeas.postprocess_outcome,
   149	          MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
   150	        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   151	        intro a _
   152	        exact hBoutcome a
   153	      have h := MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.qMatchMass_leftRight_postprocess_ge
   154	        (vectorQuantumState ψ) As Bs f
   155	      unfold qMatchMass at h
   156	      simp only [leftPlacedSubMeas_outcome, rightPlacedSubMeas_outcome] at h
   157	      simpa only [hAoutcome, hBoutcome, hApost, hBpost,
   158	        leftTensor_mul_rightTensor_eq_opTensor,
   159	        vectorQuantumState_ev_eq_stateQForm, MIPStarRE.QPBT.heteroKron] using h

   161	/-- Squared effects in one measurement fiber sum to at most the identity. -/
   162	private theorem measurement_fiber_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one {α β ι : Type*}
   163	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   164	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (α × β) ι) (a : α) :
   165	    ∑ b : β, (M.effect (a, b))ᴴ * M.effect (a, b) ≤ 1 := by
   166	  classical
   167	  have hsquare_le (z : α × β) :
   168	      (M.effect z)ᴴ * M.effect z ≤ M.effect z := by
   169	    rw [measurement_effect_hermitian M z]
   170	    exact MIPStarRE.Quantum.sq_le_self (M.pos z) (measurement_effect_le_one M z)
   171	  calc
   172	    ∑ b : β, (M.effect (a, b))ᴴ * M.effect (a, b) ≤
   173	        ∑ b : β, M.effect (a, b) :=
   174	      Finset.sum_le_sum fun b _ => hsquare_le (a, b)
   175	    _ ≤ ∑ a' : α, ∑ b : β, M.effect (a', b) :=
   176	      Finset.single_le_sum
   177	        (fun a' _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ => M.pos (a', b))
   178	        (Finset.mem_univ a)
   179	    _ = ∑ z : α × β, M.effect z := (Fintype.sum_prod_type _).symm
   180	    _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one

   182	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for approximate commutation at paper
   183	lines 410--461: a left-placed measurement fiber is square-summable. -/
   184	theorem left_fiber_contraction {α β ιA ιB : Type*}
   185	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   186	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   187	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (α × β) ιA) (a : α) :
   188	    (1 - ∑ b : β, (leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) (M.effect (a, b)))ᴴ *
   189	      leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) (M.effect (a, b))).PosSemidef := by
   190	  apply Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp
   191	  rw [sub_nonneg]
   192	  calc
   193	    ∑ b : β, (leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) (M.effect (a, b)))ᴴ *
   194	          leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) (M.effect (a, b)) =
   195	        ∑ b : β, leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB)
   196	          ((M.effect (a, b))ᴴ * M.effect (a, b)) := by
   197	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   198	      intro b _
   199	      rw [leftTensor_conjTranspose, leftTensor_mul_leftTensor]
   200	    _ = leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB)
   201	        (∑ b : β, (M.effect (a, b))ᴴ * M.effect (a, b)) :=
   202	      leftTensor_finset_sum Finset.univ _
   203	    _ ≤ leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) (1 : Op ιA) :=
   204	      leftTensor_mono (measurement_fiber_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one M a)
   205	    _ = 1 := leftTensor_one

   207	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for approximate commutation at paper
   208	lines 410--461: a right-placed measurement fiber is square-summable. -/
   209	theorem right_fiber_contraction {α β ιA ιB : Type*}
   210	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   211	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   212	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (α × β) ιB) (a : α) :
   213	    (1 - ∑ b : β, (rightTensor (ι₁ := ιA) (M.effect (a, b)))ᴴ *
   214	      rightTensor (ι₁ := ιA) (M.effect (a, b))).PosSemidef := by
   215	  apply Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp
   216	  rw [sub_nonneg]
   217	  calc
   218	    ∑ b : β, (rightTensor (ι₁ := ιA) (M.effect (a, b)))ᴴ *
   219	          rightTensor (ι₁ := ιA) (M.effect (a, b)) =
   220	        ∑ b : β, rightTensor (ι₁ := ιA)
   221	          ((M.effect (a, b))ᴴ * M.effect (a, b)) := by
   222	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl

    18	/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    19	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    20	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    21	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    22	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    23	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    24	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    25	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    26	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    27	      if a = b then 0 else
    28	        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
    29	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)
    30	
    31	/-- The quantitative relation in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    32	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    33	def IsConsistentWithin {X α ι : Type*}
    34	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    35	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    36	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    37	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
    38	  consistencyDefect μ A B ψ ≤ δ
    39	
    40	/-- Unit-alphabet specialization of `def:povm-distance`, blueprint
    41	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    42	noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    43	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    44	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    45	  opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x) (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ
    46	
    47	/-- The unit-alphabet operator distance equals its one-outcome family form from
    48	`def:povm-distance`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper
    49	`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    50	theorem opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    51	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    52	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    53	    opDistSq μ M N ψ = opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x)
    54	      (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ := rfl
    55	
    56	/-- The strategy-distance relation `def:strategy-distance`. The two strategies'
    57	local Hilbert spaces are identified, and both measurement distances are
    58	evaluated on the first strategy's state. Blueprint
    59	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    60	structure AreCloseStrategies (G : Game) (S S' : Strategy G) (δ : ℝ) : Prop where
    61	  /-- Identification of Alice's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    62	  hA : S.ιA = S'.ιA
    63	  /-- Identification of Bob's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    64	  hB : S.ιB = S'.ιB
    65	  state : stateDistSq S.ψ (reindexState
    66	      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.cast hA).symm (Equiv.cast hB).symm) S'.ψ) ≤ δ
    67	  alice : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.fst)
    68	      (fun x a => heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1)
    69	      (fun x a => heteroKron (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hA) ((S'.A x).effect a)) 1)
    70	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    71	  bob : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.snd)
    72	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b))
    73	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hB) ((S'.B y).effect b)))
    74	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    75	
    76	end MIPStarRE.QPBT
